run_browser_automation_sse.description: Executes a browser automation task with Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming, returning a real-time event stream with automation progress, browser streaming URL, and final results.

params.name: url
params.description: Target website URL to automate.

params.name: goal
params.description: Natural language description of what to accomplish on the website. Minimum string length: 1.

params.name: browser_profile
params.description: Browser profile for execution. `lite` uses standard browser, `stealth` uses anti-detection browser.

params.name: api_integration
params.description: Name of the integration making this API call (e.g., "dify", "zapier", "n8n"). Used for analytics.

params.name: agent_config
params.description: Agent behavior configuration. Example payload shows: `mode`, `cursor_style`, `max_steps`, `max_duration_seconds`.

params.name: capture_config
params.description: Configure which data to capture during the run. Example payload shows: `elements`, `snapshots`, `screenshots`, `recording`, `html`.

params.name: webhook_url
params.description: HTTPS URL to receive webhook notifications for run lifecycle events. Must use HTTPS.

params.name: use_vault
params.description: Opt-in to vault credentials for this run. When true, enabled vault items are included. Defaults to false.

params.name: use_profile
params.description: Opt-in to the default Browser Context Profile if Browser Context Profiles are enabled; legacy callers are silently ignored when the profiles feature is disabled. Returns 400 when enabled but no default profile is set.

params.name: profile_id
params.description: Browser Context Profile ID to use when `use_profile` is true. Minimum string length: 1.

params.name: credential_item_ids
params.description: Scope vault credentials to specific credential URIs. Requires `use_vault` to be true. If omitted with `use_vault: true`, all enabled items are used. Minimum array length: 1.

params.name: proxy_config
params.description: Proxy configuration.

params.name: output_schema
params.description: Optional provider-supported structured-output schema subset for the run result. Unsupported fields are rejected before the request is accepted. Example: a JSON Schema object with `type`, `properties`, `required`.

list_runs.description: List automation runs with optional filtering by status, goal text, and date range. Returns paginated results with total count. Default sort order is newest first.

params.name: status
params.description: Filter by run status. Options: `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`.

params.name: goal
params.description: Filter runs by goal text (case-insensitive partial match). Maximum string length: 500.

params.name: created_after
params.description: Filter runs created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

params.name: created_before
params.description: Filter runs created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

params.name: sort_direction
params.description: Sort order by `created_at`. Options: `asc`, `desc`. Default: `desc`.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Cursor for pagination (from previous response).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100). Default: 20.

get_run.description: Get detailed information about a specific automation run by its ID.

params.name: id
params.description: Run ID. Path parameter. Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`.

params.name: screenshots
params.description: Screenshot delivery mode. `url`: absolute URLs to screenshot images. `base64`: inline data URIs. `none`: omit screenshots. Default: `url`.

params.name: html
params.description: HTML snapshot delivery mode. `url`: absolute URLs to HTML snapshot pages (only non-null when `capture_config.html` was enabled). `none`: omit HTML URLs. Default: `url`.

cancel_run.description: Cancel a run by ID. Only runs created via `/v1/automation/run-async` or `/v1/automation/run-sse` can be cancelled; runs created via the synchronous `/v1/automation/run` endpoint cannot be cancelled.

params.name: id
params.description: Run ID. Path parameter. Pattern: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`.

search_web.description: Search the web and get structured results, returning ranked results with titles, snippets, and URLs.

params.name: query
params.description: Search query. Length 1-2000.

params.name: purpose
params.description: Why this search is being run — the underlying goal or task the results will be used for. Used to better rank results against your intent. Length 1-2000.

params.name: location
params.description: Country code for geo-targeted results.

params.name: language
params.description: Language code for result language.

params.name: include_domains
params.description: Comma-separated list of domains to restrict results to.

params.name: exclude_domains
params.description: Comma-separated list of domains to exclude from results.

params.name: domain_type
params.description: Type of search to perform: `web` for standard results, `news` for news articles, `research_paper` for academic papers. Defaults to `web`. Options: `web`, `news`, `research_paper`.

params.name: after_date
params.description: Return results after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: before_date
params.description: Return results before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

params.name: recency_minutes
params.description: Return results from the past N minutes (1 to 5,256,000).

params.name: pub_year_min
params.description: Return research papers published on or after this year (0-9999, inclusive). Only supported for `domain_type=research_paper`.

params.name: pub_year_max
params.description: Return research papers published on or before this year (0-9999, inclusive). Only supported for `domain_type=research_paper`.

params.name: page
params.description: Page number for pagination, starting from 0 (max 10).

params.name: include_thumbnail
params.description: When `"true"`, each result includes a `thumbnail_url` when available. Defaults to false. Options: `true`, `false`.

params.name: fetch
params.description: JSON-encoded fetch configuration object. Maximum string length 256.

list_search_usage.description: List search usage records for the authenticated user, returning paginated results with query details, status, and result counts.

params.name: status
params.description: Options: `completed`, `failed`.

params.name: limit
params.description: Default 100. Required range 1-1000.

params.name: page
params.description: Default 1. Required range x >= 1.

fetch_extract_content.description: Fetches web pages, renders JavaScript-heavy pages when needed, and returns clean extracted content in your preferred format.

params.name: urls
params.description: Array of URLs to fetch (1-10). All URLs are fetched in parallel. Each URL is processed independently — if one fails, others still return successfully. Errors are reported per-URL in the `errors` array.

params.name: purpose
params.description: Why these URLs are being fetched — the underlying goal or task the content will be used for. Used to better tailor fetching and extraction to your intent. (1-2000 characters)

params.name: format
params.description: Output format for extracted content. `markdown` (default) is ideal for LLM consumption. `html` returns cleaned semantic HTML. `json` returns a structured document tree. Available options: `markdown`, `html`, `json`. Default: `markdown`.

params.name: links
params.description: Extract all outbound links from each page. Useful for discovering related pages or navigating to specific content. Links are returned as absolute URLs in the `links` array of each result. Default: `false`.

params.name: image_links
params.description: Extract all image URLs from each page. Useful for finding visual content or media assets. Image links are returned as absolute URLs in the `image_links` array of each result. Default: `false`.

params.name: page_metadata
params.description: Return page-head metadata for each page in the `page_metadata` object of each result: canonical URL, favicon, robots directive, generator, viewport, keywords, all Open Graph (`og`), Twitter card (`twitter`), and article tags, and remaining named meta tags under `other`. Useful for SEO/technical audits and link-preview generation. Default: `false`.

params.name: ttl
params.description: Caller freshness tolerance in seconds for the cached entry. Omit (default) for unlimited tolerance — any cached entry is acceptable. Set to 0 to prefer a live fetch; a cached entry is still served if the origin's `Cache-Control: max-age` covers its age, or the host is in the small allowlist of operator-pinned never-expire domains. Set to N > 0 to accept a cached entry whose age is below N; the upstream `Cache-Control: max-age` and the never-expire allowlist may extend (never shorten) this tolerance. Range: x >= 0.

params.name: per_url_timeout_ms
params.description: Wall-clock timeout budget in milliseconds applied independently to each URL. If one URL exceeds this budget, it returns a per-URL timeout error while other URLs in the same request continue. Range: 1 <= x <= 110000.

params.name: if_none_match
params.description: ETag validator from a prior fetch of this URL, forwarded verbatim as the `If-None-Match` header on the origin request. Only valid with a single URL — combining with a batch of URLs returns a 400. tf-fetch does not persist validators; the caller owns replaying them. Minimum string length: 1.

params.name: if_modified_since
params.description: Last-Modified validator from a prior fetch of this URL, forwarded verbatim as the `If-Modified-Since` header on the origin request. Only valid with a single URL — combining with a batch of URLs returns a 400. tf-fetch does not persist validators; the caller owns replaying them. Minimum string length: 1.

params.name: include_etag_and_last_modified
params.description: Opt-in to receiving `etag` / `last_modified` validators (and `not_modified` detection) on each result. Defaults to `false` — tf-fetch omits these fields unless requested. Independent of `if_none_match` / `if_modified_since`: works with a single URL or a batch.

params.name: include_selectors
params.description: Array of CSS selectors (1-20 entries, each 1-1000 characters) that scope extracted content (`text`, `links`, `image_links`) to elements matching ANY entry, concatenated in document order. Tag selectors cover semantic sections (`main`, `article`, `nav`); entries may themselves use CSS comma-grouping. Selected content is returned verbatim in the requested format (scripts/styles stripped) — automatic boilerplate removal is bypassed. Page-level metadata (`title`, `description`, `language`, `author`, `published_date`) still comes from the full document. When some entries match and others do not, the URL still succeeds and the misses are reported in the result's `unmatched_selectors`. When no entry matches anything, that URL fails with the per-URL error code `selector_not_matched` (carrying `unmatched_selectors` and `candidate_selectors` retry hints) — never a silent full-page fallback. URLs that resolve to direct PDF/CSV downloads fail with `selector_unsupported`. Invalid CSS selector syntax is rejected with a 422. Applied post-fetch: caching and routing are unchanged.

params.name: exclude_selectors
params.description: Array of CSS selectors (1-20 entries, each 1-1000 characters) for elements to remove before extraction — applied before `include_selectors` scopes what remains, so it also prunes inside selected regions. Entries may themselves use CSS comma-grouping. Entries that match nothing are a no-op, never an error, but URLs that resolve to direct PDF/CSV downloads fail with `selector_unsupported`. Invalid CSS selector syntax is rejected with a 422. Applied post-fetch: caching and routing are unchanged.
